videos.script: Six lessons in, your queries have started to get long. This is the lesson about that. {{long}} A subquery is a query inside a query, and you have already written four of them without being told what they were called — every time we wrapped something to filter on it, that was this. {{already}} What is new here is the naming. WITH lets you give each step a name and stack them, so a query reads as a sequence of small ideas instead of one expression nested five deep. Same work, same speed, and a person can follow it. {{with}} Then two things that are genuinely new. Recursive queries, which walk a tree — a category and everything under it, an employee and everybody who reports up to them — in one statement. {{recursive}} And views, which are a query stored under a name. Not data: a query. Every time you select from it, it runs. A materialised view is the other one, and that one does store the answer, which means it can be stale, and being clear about which you have is the whole skill. {{views}} There is also a piece of folklore here worth killing early. People will tell you CTEs are slow, or that they are free. Both were true of some database in some year, and the only honest answer is that you measure it — which is lesson 10. {{folklore}}
